result:
I found one real bug in `eml_parser.parser`: turning on `ignore_bad_start` corrupts every email, including well-formed ones. I tested two properties; this one failed and the other passed.

**Bug (High, Logic): `ignore_bad_start=True` merges the whole message into one header line**

The option is meant to skip junk lines at the start of a file. In `EmlParser.decode_email_bytes` (`parser.py:229-237`), two mistakes break it:
1. **Newlines are dropped.** The file is split on `b'\n'` and the lines are joined back with `_eml_file += line`, without the newlines. All headers and the body end up as one header line.
2. **The guard checks the wrong thing.** `b':' not in eml_file.split(b'\n', 1)` asks whether some line is exactly `b':'`, not whether the first line contains a colon. So it is almost always true, and the broken rebuild runs on every input.

Example:
```python
raw = b"Subject: hello\nTo: bob@example.com\n\nbody text\n"
EmlParser().decode_email_bytes(raw)                         -> {'subject': ['hello'], 'to': ['bob@example.com']}
EmlParser().decode_email_bytes(raw, ignore_bad_start=True)  -> {'subject': ['helloTo: bob@example.combody text']}
```
An input that really does start with junk (`b"garbage line\nSubject: hi\nTo: ..."`) fails the same way. Recipients, the body, attachments, and the URLs, emails and IPs normally pulled from the body are all lost without any error. The bug report includes a two-line fix: check `[0]` (the first line) and use `splitlines(keepends=True)`. I haven't applied or tested that fix.

**Passed: `string_sliding_window_loop` loses no URLs.** This function cuts long bodies into chunks before searching them. Over 500 generated bodies with URLs scattered in them, every URL found in the full body was also found in the chunks.

Files are in `runs/eml-parser_r5/work/`:
- `bug_report_eml_parser_parser_2026-10-06_04-36_thpg.md`
- `test_parser.py`
- `repro.py`
